meta.title: Payment authorization: retries and timeouts
meta.intro: How a payment request goes through an idempotency check, fraud scoring and a PSP call, and is either approved or retried. Pick a scenario and press **Next step →**.
meta.source: Generic payment design example; not the numbers of any specific PSP or company.

nodes.title: Mobile app
facts: Creates a **new key** on every tap of the pay button and reuses it when resending.

nodes.title: API gateway
facts: Checks the token and applies a per-user rate limit.

nodes.title: Payments API
facts: Takes the request and runs the steps below in order.

nodes.title: Idempotency store
facts: If the key already exists, the earlier response is returned as is.

nodes.title: Fraud scoring
facts: 70 or more is declined; 40 to 70 requires 3DS.

nodes.title: PSP router
facts: Picks a PSP from the card BIN and outage state.
On a timeout the result is **unknown**: it queries first, then retries.

nodes.title: PSP B
facts: Used only when A returns 5xx or its circuit breaker is open.

nodes.title: Retry queue
facts: Re-enqueues with exponential backoff; after 3 tries the message goes to the dead-letter queue.

nodes.title: Ledger DB
facts: Writes **PENDING** first and changes it after the PSP answers.

nodes.title: Webhook receiver
facts: Receives approvals that arrive late, after a timeout, and reconciles the ledger.

nodes.title: Ops dashboard
facts: A person reviews dead-lettered payments and refunds or reprocesses them.

scenarios.title: Approved first time
scenarios.summary: App → Payments API → PSP A → ledger
scenarios.lead: The most common path: the card payment is approved on the first attempt.

steps.title: App requests the payment
steps.what: Amount, currency, card token and `Idempotency-Key` travel in one request.
steps.where: The gateway checks the JWT and forwards it to the Payments API.
steps.fail: Expired token: **401**; over the per-minute limit: **429**.

steps.title: Claim the idempotency key
steps.what: A key seen for the first time is stored and processing continues.
steps.fail: Redis down: refused with **503** to stay safe.

steps.title: Compute the fraud score
steps.what: A score from the amount, the device and recent attempts.
steps.where: The rule engine inside the payment service.
steps.fail: No answer within 300ms: require 3DS to be safe.

steps.title: Record PENDING, call the PSP
steps.what: PENDING goes into the ledger and the router sends an authorization to PSP A.
steps.where: Ledger table `payments` and PSP A's HTTPS API.
steps.fail: No answer within 3 seconds: continue in the timeout scenario.

steps.title: Approval returned
steps.what: The ledger becomes CAPTURED and the app gets a 200.
steps.fail: Ledger update fails: the response still succeeds and the webhook repairs it.

scenarios.title: PSP timeout and retry
scenarios.summary: PSP A silent → queue → retry → PSP B
scenarios.lead: PSP A does not answer within 3 seconds, so the payment goes through the retry queue to PSP B.

steps.title: PSP A does not answer
steps.what: The router waits 3 seconds and gives up. At this point **nobody knows whether it was approved**.
steps.fail: Retrying blindly could charge twice, so the router queries PSP A first.

steps.title: Put it on the retry queue
steps.what: A message with a 1 second delay; the app gets `202 PENDING`.

steps.title: Run the retry
steps.what: The same `Idempotency-Key` goes to PSP B.
steps.fail: PSP B fails too: a second retry after 4 seconds.

steps.title: PSP B approves
steps.what: The ledger becomes CAPTURED and the app gets a push notification.
steps.where: The app learns the result by polling or push.
steps.fail: A lost push is caught by polling.

scenarios.title: Late approval webhook
scenarios.summary: PSP A approves after the timeout
scenarios.lead: PSP B has already approved after the timeout when PSP A sends a late approval webhook.

steps.title: PSP A's late webhook
steps.what: PSP A's approval arrives right after the timeout.
steps.where: The webhook receiver, after checking the signature.

steps.title: Check against the ledger
steps.what: Already CAPTURED: PSP A's approval is marked **to be voided**.
steps.fail: Reconciliation fails: sent to the dead-letter queue.

steps.title: Alert an operator
steps.what: The double approval appears on the ops dashboard.
steps.fail: A missed alert is caught by the daily reconciliation.

scenarios.title: Declined by fraud scoring
scenarios.lead: The fraud score is high, so the payment is declined without calling a PSP.

steps.title: Accept the request, claim the key
steps.what: The key is claimed first, as on the normal path.

steps.title: Fraud score 85
steps.what: 70 or more: the payment is declined.
steps.fail: A false positive needs a manual release by support.

steps.title: Decline response
steps.what: No PSP call: DECLINED goes into the ledger and the app gets the answer.
steps.fail: Retrying with the same key returns **the same decline**.

tldr.title: Summary
points: A timeout is not a failure, it is **unknown**: query first, then retry.
At most **3 retries**; after that a person takes over.
